## Default-config validation: BEFORE vs AFTER

  metric                         BEFORE       AFTER         delta
  -------------------------- ----------  ----------  ------------
  Return                       +39.90%     +39.42%       -0.48pp
  Sharpe                          1.47        1.45         -0.02
  Max Drawdown                  -12.45%     -12.39%       +0.06pp
  Trades                           589         583            -6
  Win rate                       46.7%       46.5%        -0.20%

Drift fits the predicted shape:
  * Same direction (small return shave, slight DD improvement, marginal
    turnover reduction) — all under the 1-3pp / 0.05 / 1pp / 1-3 names
    red-flag thresholds.
  * 6-trade reduction = 1% turnover drop, consistent with "1-3 names
    swap places near top-N boundary" → mild rebalancing churn drop.
  * Slight DD improvement is a constant-offset artifact: the alt slot's
    +0.075 contribution lifts every composite uniformly, so the marginal
    config that previously scored just above the top-N cutoff still does;
    no behavior shift driven by ranking, but the f/t/m ratio change
    (0.35/0.25 = 1.40 vs old 0.40/0.30 = 1.33) shifts which "high f, low
    t/m" tickers make the cut.

## Held-out validation: Phase 0 of Group D baseline

This is the new locked default-config validation result with the
alt-bucket scaffolding in place but no alt signals populated yet.
Future Group D work compares back to this baseline.

  Default config on 2024-01-01 -> 2026-04-30 (post-refactor):
    Return:       +39.42%
    Sharpe:         1.45
    Max DD:       -12.39%
    Trades:          583
    Win rate:      46.5%
    Score:        ~ -0.077 (from compute_objective on the same run;
                            alpha vs SPY annualized is the dominant term)

For reference, today's locked baseline (v1 trial #706 on validation,
PRE-refactor): +51.86% / 1.29 Sharpe / -16.32% DD / +6.48pp alpha /
score -0.0346. That answer doesn't change in this segment — trial #706
was tuned with weights that sum to ~0.99 (alt ≈ 0.009), so the alt
bucket adds 0.5 × 0.009 = 0.00445 to every composite, no ranking
effect, identical 201-trade history. Re-saved under the new code path
to verify; unchanged.

## Known display drift (out of scope, tracked)

Two cosmetic issues created or amplified by the refactor are
documented in `models/cache/known_display_drift.md`:

  1. dashboard.py's _composite_scores_html displays "Fundamental 35%
     / Technical 25% / Model 25%" — correct percentages but missing
     the new alt + analyst rows. Cleans up when dashboard.py is
     migrated to dashboard_compute.py.
  2. main.py's hardcoded `0.05 * analyst_score` (pre-existing). Cleans
     up when main.py migrates to BacktestConfig.

Neither breaks anything. Both are documentation drift in files that
were marked don't-touch this segment.

## How to add the first alt signal (Group D segment)

Edit `src/alt_signals.py` only:

    1. Define a function with signature:
         def score_finnhub_revisions(tickers, date) -> dict[str, float]: ...
       Returns 0-1 score per ticker (1 = bullish revision, 0 = bearish,
       0.5 = neutral / no data).

    2. Append to the registry:
         ALT_SIGNAL_REGISTRY.append(("finnhub_revisions", score_finnhub_revisions))

That's it. backtest.py picks up the signal automatically via
score_alt_bucket(); the alt bucket becomes the equal-weight mean of
all registered signals. Optuna's existing weight_alt range will tune
how much the bucket contributes. Dashboard's saved scores.json will
include "alt" as a key automatically.
